column1: # Daily flow rows deleted rather than published as a clamped zero, because
# the deficit each row's raw negative revision opens is fully discharged by
# the very next row -- so deleting the row does exactly what the next row's
# `days_covered` already states in the pipeline, and camdl reads that window
# from row spacing alone (docs/camdl-data-spec.md:606-624 in the modelling
# repo: "a hole still closes an incidence bin"; deleting instead leaves the
# bin open across the gap). `emit_daily` in build_streams.py checks each
# entry against the built series before honouring it: the named row must
# exist, must not be the first or last row of its stream, and its carried
# value must be exactly 0 -- if a later re-extraction changes any of that,
# the build stops rather than silently deleting the wrong thing.
# AN ENTRY NAMES ONE ROW. This is not a rule the build applies on discovery.
# `revisions.tsv` carries other raw-negative clamps of the same shape --
# `cases_daily_nord_kivu` and `deaths_daily_nord_kivu`, 2026-06-11 -- that are
# NOT listed here and are still published as a plain carried zero, because
# nobody has decided yet whether to extend this treatment to them. See
# `data-agent-channel.md`, 2026-09-03, for the reasoning behind the three
# rows below and the open question about the pair left out.
# COLUMNS
#   stream        the daily stream file stem
#   column        the observation column inside it
#   time          the date whose row is deleted
#   verified_by   who decided, and when
#   note          the arithmetic that licenses dropping this specific row
